chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Abu Ayyub, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said:

"I'tikaf cannot be for less than three days. Whoever performs i'tikaf must fast, and it is appropriate for the one performing i'tikaf, when he enters i'tikaf, to make a stipulation just as the one who enters ihram makes a stipulation."

key_terms.الِاعْتِكَافُ: i'tikaf, the act of spiritual retreat in worship
key_terms.ثَلَاثَةِ أَيَّامٍ: three days, the minimum valid period mentioned here
key_terms.صَامَ: fasted, indicating the requirement of sawm during i'tikaf
key_terms.يَشْتَرِطَ: to make a stipulation or condition at the beginning
key_terms.يُحْرِمُ: enters into ihram for hajj or 'umrah

ai.seo_question: What is the minimum duration of i'tikaf and is fasting required during it?
ai.summary: This hadith gives legal rulings for i'tikaf, stating that its minimum duration is three days and that fasting is required for the one observing it. It also instructs the mu'takif to make a stipulation at the outset, similar to the stipulation made by one entering ihram.
